extracted.intended_audience: PTAB judges and staff, USPTO management and personnel, and practitioners/parties involved in PTAB proceedings or filing appeals and FOIA requests
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and binding standards governing pre-issuance circulation and review of PTAB panel decisions, limits on Office and management involvement, judicial review/appeal filing and timing requirements, and USPTO FOIA disclosure/request processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Director and senior officials communicating with panel pre-issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to issuance of a decision by a panel, the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, and Commissioner for Trademarks shall not communicate, directly or through intermediaries, with any member of the panel regarding the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition is categorical except where the individual is also a member of the panel (see exception). It forbids any pre-issuance influence or direction aimed at a panel's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when Director or senior official is a panel member
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition on communications does not apply to any individual listed above who is a member of the panel; when sitting as a member the Director or other individual is a coequal member and exercises no review authority over the proceeding prior to issuance of the panel’s decision on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such individuals sit on the panel they have the same status and responsibilities as other panel members; they are not supervisors for pre-issuance review purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted communications about resources or procedural status
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the limits on communications prevents the Director (or Management Judge) or delegates from communicating with a panel as to resource needs or the procedural status of any proceeding pending before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications that are strictly about resources or procedural status (not substantive aspects of the decision) are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel designation and limits on Director direction of paneling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Administrative Patent Judge or delegates shall designate panels on behalf of the Director only in accordance with public Board paneling guidance. The Director may issue generally applicable paneling guidance but shall not direct or otherwise influence the paneling or repaneling of any specific proceeding prior to issuance of the panel decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director-level guidance must be general and public; specific case paneling decisions must follow public Board paneling guidance and cannot be directed by the Director prior to issuance. Review/rehearing scenarios allow repaneling via Order consistent with public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited pre-issuance involvement by Management Judges and Office employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as requested (see next metric) or permitted by other specified exceptions, prior to issuance of a decision no Management Judge or an officer or employee of the Office external to the Board shall initiate communication, directly or through intermediaries, with any member of a panel regarding the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management Judges and external Office staff must refrain from initiating pre-issuance communications with panel members about decisions unless exceptions apply; this preserves panel autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel-member-requested input from Management Judges or external Office employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual panel member may request that one or more Management Judges or an officer or employee of the Office external to the Board provide input on a decision prior to issuance. The choice to request input is optional and solely within the discretion of an individual panel member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input must be requested by a panel member; it is not to be imposed. The panel member controls whether to solicit outside input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel final authority over content and optional adoption of edits
rubrics_metrics.description: It is within the sole discretion of the panel to adopt any edits, suggestions, or feedback provided to the panel by Management Judges or Office employees as part of a requested review. The panel has final authority and responsibility for the content of a decision and determines whether and how to incorporate any feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any edits or feedback provided under a requested review are advisory only; panels retain ultimate responsibility for decisions and may accept, modify, or reject outside suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Judge equal status when sitting as panel member
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition on pre-issuance communications does not apply to any Management Judge who is a member of the panel. When sitting as a member of a panel, a Management Judge is a coequal member of the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management Judges who are actual panel members may engage normally as panel colleagues; the restriction is against external initiation of contact by Management Judges who are not panel members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on post-circulation review by Management Judges if internal review procedures establish non-Management reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office establishes procedures governing internal circulation and review of decisions to designated members of the Board (non-Management Judges), no Management Judge or an officer or employee external to the Board shall participate directly or indirectly in such review, and the reviewing non-Management Judges shall not discuss the substance of any circulated decision with a Management Judge prior to issuance of the decision (except with a Management Judge who is a member of the panel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviews are assigned to non-Management Judges, Management involvement is barred to preserve independence; discussions of circulated substantive material with Management Judges are prohibited except where the Management Judge is a panel member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonexistence of unwritten or non-public binding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions of the Board are expected to comport with applicable statutes, regulations, binding case law, and written Office policy and guidance. There shall be no unwritten Office or Board policy or guidance that is binding on any panel of the Board. All written policy and guidance binding on panels of the Board shall be made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binding directives must be in writing and publicly available; panels must follow statutes, regs, case law, and written public policy only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of appeal — methods and receipt date
rubrics_metrics.description: For an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141, the notice of appeal required by 35 U.S.C. 142 must be filed with the Director by electronic mail to the email address indicated on USPTO's Office of the General Counsel web page; this electronically submitted notice will be accorded a receipt date in Eastern Time when received. If email cannot be used, submission may be by Priority Mail Express® to the Office of the Solicitor at the specified address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the notice must also be filed with PTAB in the appropriate manner per §§41.10(a),(b) or 42.6(b). Parties must follow the designated email address and alternate physical mailing procedure if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with federal appellate procedure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In all appeals, the party initiating the appeal must comply with the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure and Rules for the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, including serving the requisite number of copies on the Court and paying the requisite fee for the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the notice of appeal with the Director does not relieve the party of complying with court rules on service and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional service/content requirements for appeals from particular proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In appeals arising out of an ex parte reexamination ordered pursuant to §1.525, notice must be served as provided in §1.550(f). In appeals arising out of an inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, or a derivation proceeding, the notice must provide sufficient information to allow the Director to determine whether to exercise the right to intervene pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 143, and must be served as provided in §42.6(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific types of proceedings carry additional service or content obligations for the notice of appeal so the Director (and Office) can assess intervention rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of election filing requirements under 35 U.S.C. 141(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of election to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 146 instead of 35 U.S.C. 141 must be filed with the Director by electronic mail to the Office of the General Counsel address (receipt date in Eastern Time), and a copy must also be filed with PTAB in the manner provided in §42.6(b) and served where necessary pursuant to §42.6(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same electronic-first filing protocol and ensure copies and service per the cited PTAB rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing complaint copies for civil action under 35 U.S.C. 146
rubrics_metrics.description: The party initiating an action under 35 U.S.C. 146 must file a copy of the complaint no later than five business days after filing the complaint in district court with the PTAB in the manner provided in §42.6(b), and with the Office of the Solicitor pursuant to §104.2; failure to comply can result in further action within USPTO consistent with the final Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely transmittal of complaint copies to the Office and PTAB is mandatory and has potential consequences if omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing appeals and civil actions (63-day rule) and computation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal under 35 U.S.C. 142 must be filed no later than sixty-three (63) days after the date of the final Board decision. A civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 must be commenced no later than sixty-three (63) days after the final Board decision. A timely request for rehearing will reset the time to 63 days after action on that rehearing; subsequent rehearing requests from the same party generally will not reset the time unless permitted by Board order. If the last day falls on a Federal holiday in D.C., time is extended pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 21(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must track 63-day deadlines, rehearing effects, and holiday extensions carefully to preserve rights to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time for appeal or civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (or designee) may extend the time for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action upon written request if the request is filed before expiration and shows good cause, or if filed after expiration and shows the failure to act was the result of excusable neglect. Requests must be filed by electronic mail to the OG Counsel address (or by Priority Mail Express if email cannot be used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are discretionary and require written showing of good cause or excusable neglect; use the specified filing channels to preserve the request's receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Officer role and FOIA general policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The information in Part 102 is furnished to guide the public and complies with FOIA. The FOIA Officer is the USPTO employee designated to administer FOIA; correspondence should be addressed to the FOIA Officer at the specified mailing or delivery address. USPTO's policy is to make discretionary disclosures of records exempt from disclosure when disclosure would not foreseeably harm an interest protected by a FOIA exemption (but this policy does not create a court-enforceable right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests and communications should be directed to the FOIA Officer; the Office favors discretionary disclosure where no harm is foreseeably caused but this is not a legal entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reference facility and indexes — content and update frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO maintains a public reference facility that contains records FOIA requires to be made regularly available for public inspection and copying; the FOIA Officer shall maintain and make available a current subject-matter index of the public inspection facility records, updated regularly, at least quarterly for newly included records. Records created on or after November 1, 1996 shall be made available electronically through USPTO's web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public reference facility and electronic indexes are the primary means for routine public access; indexes should be updated at least quarterly and electronic availability is required for post-1996 records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of records maintained for public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO maintains and makes available for public inspection: (1) a current index identifying matters issued/adopted/promulgated after July 4, 1967; (2) copies of released records likely to be re-requested; (3) a general index of such records; (4) final opinions and orders (including concurring/dissenting opinions); (5) statements of policy and interpretations adopted by USPTO not published in the Federal Register; and (6) administrative staff manuals and instructions to staff that affect a member of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories specify discrete classes of documents for routine public inspection and copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA records scope and obligation to create records
rubrics_metrics.description: Records under FOIA include all Government records regardless of format, including electronic records, audio/video, and photographs. There is no obligation to create, compile, or obtain records to satisfy a FOIA request. For electronic data, USPTO shall undertake reasonable efforts to search for information in electronic format when responding to requests where creation or extraction issues arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters cannot compel creation of new records under FOIA; USPTO must reasonably search existing electronic records and may create information only pursuant to user-fee statutes or other lawful authority (which is outside FOIA). Correspondence and copies of requested records must be preserved until authorized disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for making FOIA requests — content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for USPTO records not customarily made available must be in writing and processed under FOIA, addressed to the FOIA Officer. Requests should describe records with enough detail (date, title/author/recipient/subject, office location, case title/court) to enable USPTO to locate them with reasonable effort. Requests for records about another individual require written authorization signed by that individual or proof of death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More specific requests increase likelihood of successful retrieval; if the FOIA Officer determines a request is insufficiently descriptive they will tell the requester what additional information is needed and may offer to discuss modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and scope for responding to FOIA requests including consultations and referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOIA Officer will process FOIA requests directed to USPTO and include only records within USPTO's possession and control as of the date the FOIA Officer receives the request. If another federal agency has the primary interest in a record, the FOIA Officer shall refer the record to that agency for direct response and ordinarily notify the requester of the referral. Consultations shall be handled according to the date the FOIA request was received by the first agency; agreements may be made to eliminate the need for consultations/referrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding to a request focuses on records USPTO controls at receipt; referrals and consultations are used when other agencies have primary or significant interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits, unusual circumstances, and multitrack processing for FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOIA Officer ordinarily shall respond in order of receipt. An initial response shall be made within 20 working days of receipt of a request and an appeal decided within 20 working days of receipt by the Office of the General Counsel. In unusual circumstances (need to search field facilities, voluminous records, or need for consultation), the FOIA Officer may extend time limits by notifying the requester; extensions may not exceed a total of 10 working days unless requester agrees or other accommodation is arranged. The FOIA Officer may use two or more processing tracks (e.g., simple vs complex) and may offer slower-track requesters an opportunity to limit scope to qualify for faster processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual circumstances are narrowly defined; predictable workload alone is not an unusual circumstance absent reasonable progress. Multiple related requests may be aggregated if they constitute a single request involving unusual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing criteria and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests and appeals shall be expedited (taken out of order) when they involve: (i) imminent threat to life or physical safety, (ii) loss of substantial due process rights, (iii) widespread and exceptional media interest raising questions about Government integrity affecting public confidence, or (iv) an urgency to inform the public about actual or alleged Federal Government activity when made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information. A requester must submit a statement, certified true to the best of their knowledge, explaining the basis for expedited treatment. Determination shall be made within ten calendar days; if granted the request will be processed as soon as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification formality may be waived administratively; news media requesters who are not full-time must show main professional activity is information dissemination and demonstrate particular urgency beyond general public right to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to FOIA requests — grants and adverse determination content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is granted in whole or part the FOIA Officer will notify the requester in writing, inform of any fees, and disclose records upon payment. For adverse determinations (withhold in whole/part, nonexistence/cannot locate, not a record, format issues, fee denial, or expedited processing denial), the denial letter must be signed by the FOIA Officer and include: (1) name and title of denying official; (2) brief statement of reasons including applicable FOIA exemption(s); (3) an estimate of volume withheld (unless infeasible or harmful); and (4) a statement that the denial may be appealed and list appeal filing requirements under §102.10(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial letters must contain specific, signed information to permit meaningful administrative appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of business information obtained from submitters and notice/objection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Business information (commercial/financial info obtained from a submitter) will be disclosed under FOIA only under this section. Submitters should designate portions considered protected from disclosure (designation expires in 10 years unless justification for longer period provided). The FOIA Officer shall provide prompt written notice to submitters when a FOIA request seeks their business information (except limited exceptions) to allow seven working days to submit a detailed statement of objections specifying all grounds for withholding under FOIA including, for exemption 4, why the info is a trade secret or privileged/confidential. Failure to respond within seven working days will be treated as no objection. If the FOIA Officer decides to disclose over objection, the FOIA Officer must give written notice stating reasons, description of the information, and that disclosure will occur seven working days after submitter receives the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must mark/designate confidential business information timely; they get an opportunity to justify confidentiality with specific legal grounds. The FOIA Officer must follow notice and waiting-period procedures before disclosing business information over objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to notice requirements for submitter business information
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice requirements to submitters shall not apply if: (1) the FOIA Officer determines the information should not be disclosed; (2) the information has been lawfully published or officially made available to the public; or (3) disclosure is required by statute or by a regulation issued in accordance with Executive Order 12600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the FOIA Officer makes these determinations, the usual submitter-notice and wait processes do not apply.
